candidate.user_input: Compare permitted cabin upgrades for domestic versus international flights, including conditions for the international business-class exception. Preserve continuous-flight duration and trip-purpose qualifiers.
candidate.reference: Domestic flights over 5 hours allow booking the next class up from standard economy below business class. International flights over 5 hours allow the same upgrade. For international flights exceeding 8 hours and frequent travelers (3+ trips per quarter), business class is permitted for specific trip purposes: meeting customers, speaking engagements, or representing GitLab at conferences.

evidence.quote: For domestic flights with a duration greater than 5 hours of consecutive flight time (each segment must be 5+ hours), team members are authorized to book the next class up from standard economy as long as it is below business class.
evidence.contribution: Defines domestic flight upgrade policy for flights over 5 hours.

evidence.quote:
For international flights with a duration greater than 5 hours of consecutive flight time (each segment must be 5+ hours), team members are authorized to book the next class up from standard economy as long as it is below business class.
- Flights exceeding 8 hours of consecutive flight time - For those who travel frequently, defined as 3 or more trips per quarter internationally on flights of 8 hrs+ continuous flight time (minimum 6 flight segments with 8+ hours per segment), business class is permitted when traveling for any of the following reasons:
  - Meeting with customers
  - Speaking engagement
  - Representing GitLab at a conference
evidence.contribution: Defines international flight upgrade policy and business class exception for frequent travelers on long flights with specific trip purposes.

candidate.connection: Both contexts specify upgrade rules based on consecutive flight time; international context adds a business class exception for frequent travelers with qualifying trip purposes.
